gen-megrim-gf-stack-sans-text: Megrim draws hairline-thin, angular letters that look like they were etched for a spaceship console. Stack Sans Text follows in sturdy, big-bodied lowercase with a marker-like line, giving the sharp heading something solid to lean on.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sarpanch: Stencil-cut and loud, Wallpoet towers over Sarpanch, a plain sans whose open e keeps things friendly. Giving the heading generous size and letting the body stay modest would suit how tightly Sarpanch packs its lines.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Warnes spaces its letters wide and tapers every ink stroke to a point, with no brushy swell anywhere. Schibsted Grotesk sits beneath it with big open bowls on the e and a, so a modest body size still feels generous.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-stack-sans-headline:
Mystery Quest has a bookish, old-storybook air, with open curves and compact ascenders.

Stack Sans Headline replaces that nostalgia with a thin wire-like line and wide gaps, so the text underneath feels modern and crisp against the heading's vintage charm.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-albert-sans: Chubbo looks drawn with a fat marker tip, all smooth bends and casual warmth. And Albert Sans, a sans-serif with uniform strokes and apertures that stay open small, tidies things up without losing the friendliness.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-ibm-plex-sans: Crisp and confident, Red Hat Display draws a marker-like line with daylight showing inside every curve. Red Hat leads with punch; IBM Plex Sans handles the quieter, technical reading.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-shippori-antique: Shippori Antique reads in one uniform line, its bowls opening wide like a tipped ladle, never fussy. Oswald brings the muscle up top; the body just gets on with talking.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-sen: Commanding from the first glance, Unica One pairs a very large lowercase eye with uniform strokes and visible daylight inside each curve. Sen answers in tall, modern sans-serif lowercase, and that tall build is what makes the two feel related yet distinct.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sono: Sono, a plain sans with tall lowercase and generous default letter spacing, takes the reading while the heading speaks up. Wallpoet gets the bold, stencil-like voice above it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-sintony: Expressive and bold, Warnes cuts every stroke to a single width and stretches its spacing out wide. Sintony then offers a chunky, tall midzone in sans-serif, so curves read smoothly beneath that stretched-out heading.
